newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK SFC grants Emperor Int'l Exchange forex licence.
newsitem.headline: HK SFC grants Emperor Int'l Exchange forex licence.

text.p: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) said on Wednesday it has granted Emperor International Exchange (Hong Kong) Co Ltd a leveraged foreign exchange licence.
Emperor was the last of a batch of applicants to receive a licence after the enactment of the Leveraged Foreign Exchange Trading Ordinance in September 1994, an SFC spokesman said.

"The processing time required for dealing with Emperor International Exchange's application was due to the sheer size of the organisation and the 700 plus individual applications submitted with it," the SFC said in a statement.

Under the ordinance, foreign exchange trading companies and their representatives must apply for licences separately. The SFC, the territory's securities watchdog, issued more than 40 licences, although only 25 of the companies were still operating, including Emperor, the spokesman said.

The SFC said it took into account representations by Emperor about its fitness to be licensed, adding that the company had implemented a range of measures to improve its management and internal controls since the submission of its application.
